over_scope.reason: Judged and inside scope. The four-helper extraction of `analyze_builtin` (_extract_functions_for, _nesting_depth_for, _scan_lines_for, _function_metrics) is not literally named in the goal, but it is forced: today's `analyze_builtin` measures cognitive 20 > 15 and nesting_depth 13 > 3 on the frozen gate (I re-measured both), the gate is diff-scoped, so editing it in place surfaces BLOCKING findings, and the run's constraints say a gate finding is fixed by a behaviour-preserving refactor and never by moving the bar. The extraction is behaviour-preserving (metric key insertion order is unchanged, so JSON output ordering is identical) and every new helper measures under every threshold. No task touches run_state.py truncation limits, schema_version, CAPS/BUDGET_STAGE_FLOOR, any threshold VALUE, stage tracking, prior runs' docs, or test_dashboard_server.py indentation. Task 3 adds no product code. The JS/cbrace half is correctly left to the next slice.

residual: P2: `_scan_lines_for`'s fall-back is a FOURTH uncovered new statement, not one of the three the implementer's concern list names, and it is the guard that keeps the masked body slice aligned with the raw body slice (the invariant that stops a metric rising). Nothing executes it: it fires only when `_strip_for_scan(...).splitlines()` and `source.splitlines()` disagree, which needs a character that `str.splitlines()` breaks on but `str.split("\n")` does not (\x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85, U+2028) inside a masked span. grep for those escapes in test_quality_gate.py returns 0 hits, and I measured 0 of the 28 tree files the differential harness walks producing a mismatch, so the harness does not reach it either. conventions.md's rule of thumb and the plan's Task 4 step 5 both require an executing test in the SAME slice for every new line in this file.

P2: The 'every failure path returns the raw text' property is empirical, not structural. `_token_mask_spans` indexes `rows[row - 1]` with no bounds guard and `_mask_python_literals` wraps none of the span arithmetic in a try, so an unexpected IndexError (or any non-tokenizer exception) escapes `_strip_for_scan` into `analyze_builtin`, which `_measure_files` calls without a try/except. An escape does not fall back to raw - it kills the gate with a traceback and exit status 1, and agents/verifier.md documents exit 1 as 'measured failure', so a machine failure would be reported to the loop as a quality violation. I could not reproduce an escape (60,000 fuzzed inputs over quotes, f-strings, triple quotes, backslash continuations, NUL, BOM, \r, \x0b, \x0c, \x85, U+2028 raised nothing uncaught; the exotic-linebreak cases all fell back cleanly), so this is hardening of a claim rather than a known bug - which is why it is P2 and why the confidence on reachability is low.

P3: Two of `_scan_tokens`' three guards are unreachable through `tokenize.generate_tokens`, so they are dead defensive code that cannot receive the executing test the plan's Task 4 step 5 and conventions.md demand. Measured: of 10,025 fuzz inputs that tokenized without raising, zero produced an empty token list and zero produced a last token whose type is not ENDMARKER (the generator either raises - already caught - or terminates with ENDMARKER). The docstring's 'or a non-default end state' therefore describes a state the stdlib does not produce.

P3: Masking adds a new output side effect the gate never had: tokenizing an analyzed file emits SyntaxWarning to the gate's stderr for invalid escape sequences in f-strings, with a misleading `<string>:N` location instead of the analyzed path. Reproduced: analyzing `def f(a):\n    return f"\\{a}"\n` prints `<string>:2: SyntaxWarning: "\}" is an invalid escape sequence...` to stderr while the JSON report goes to stdout. Harmless for a caller that reads stdout only (which is what agents/verifier.md documents), but a verifier agent reading combined output now sees warning text interleaved with a gate run.

P3: The new `unmasked(text, lang)` helper's docstring contains the word 'for' ('Identity stand-in for qg._strip_for_scan...'), and two new module-level banner comments contain branch-scan keywords as ordinary English words -- 'case' in quality_gate.py:439 ('the worst case remains today's over-count') and 'for' in test_quality_gate.py:42 ('Fixtures for the scan mask'). This is the literal pattern the run's shared constraints ask every slice to avoid ('keep control-flow words ... OUT of your own new string literals and docstrings, because today's gate still counts them as branches'). I replayed the frozen pre-run gate (`git show 299f0db:.../quality_gate.py`) over both changed files with the actual diff's changed-ranges and confirmed zero over-threshold findings result (the banner comments sit at module scope outside any extracted function's span, and `unmasked`'s body is trivial enough that one extra 'for' hit does not approach cyclomatic 10 / cognitive 15), so this is not build-blocking. It is a precise but low-impact deviation from an explicit rule, filed for completeness rather than because it changes the gate's verdict.
